chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Yahya al-Halabi from Ayub ibn al-Hurr from Abu Basir said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The wage of the singer who escorts the brides is permissible, provided she is not the type of woman upon whom men enter (i.e., engage in sexual relations or is exposed to them in a manner implying prostitution).'

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no harm in it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is the salary of a female wedding singer halal or haram in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in the chapter of earnings (Makasib), clarifying that the permissibility of the singer's wage hinges on the preservation of modesty and the absence of illicit sexual exposure (zina) rather than the profession itself. This distinction reflects the Shia juristic approach of evaluating the specific context of performance and social interaction to determine the purity of income.
